extracted.intended_audience: aspiring creators of math explanatory videos, Manim users, translators/contributors, and educators interested in 3Blue1Brown-style exposition
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policies for producing visual, pedagogical math videos and related assets (animations, subtitles, dubs), including tool choice (Manim), pedagogical ordering, production quality, licensing, and contribution processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical goal: foster deep understanding and love of math
rubrics_metrics.description: Make more people love math, whether for its utility or its beauty, with the belief that such love begins with deep understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus explanations on building genuine understanding rather than rote presentation; aim for visuals and pedagogy that invite appreciation of math's beauty as well as utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool choice: use Manim when programmatic visuals fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Manim is a programmatic animation engine designed for creating longer scenes in an object-oriented environment, optimized for smoothness and a clean default style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If writing code for visuals feels liberating and your visuals benefit from precision, loops and abstraction, Manim is a good fit. If you want a GUI or lower friction, consider Desmos, GeoGebra, or other tools. For lots of non-mathematical animations, consider Blender or After Effects. The Community Edition of Manim is recommended for most users; the author's version is more experimental/testing-ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manim workflow: build clips, edit externally
rubrics_metrics.description: Manim is intended for making individual clips to be edited together later rather than for full video editing/syncing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use traditional video-editing software for tasks like syncing narration and assembling clips; avoid relying on Manim as an all-in-one editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just start (iterate and get feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin iterating and receiving feedback rather than overthinking before launching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start making and releasing content to learn through practice; iterate based on audience response instead of trying to perfect everything before the first release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete before abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Give examples before general frameworks; open with the key exercise rather than putting it at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical order should often be the reverse of logical order for learners: populate students' minds with concrete examples first, then build the general framework from those examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic choice matters more than production quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting the right topic is more important than high production values when getting started.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That said, basic production quality matters—especially audio: get a good microphone and learn how to use it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio quality: get a good microphone and learn it
rubrics_metrics.description: Good audio is essential and worth prioritizing; many videos suffered from poor audio early on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in a decent microphone and learn recording techniques; poor audio can undermine otherwise strong content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be niche
rubrics_metrics.description: Especially when starting, embrace something ultra-specific to what you care about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Niche topics create grateful early viewers and even very specific ideas can find sizable audiences online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand what role your channel/content plays (student documenting learning, expert conveying knowledge, teacher for school students, journalist summarizing breakthroughs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different genres imply different pacing and style; avoid pattern-matching from creators outside your genre since what works for one role may not work for another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never start with definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: In math, definitions should not be seen as a starting point but rather as an ending point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay formal definitions until students have seen motivating examples and have some intuition; use definitions after building context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be visual
rubrics_metrics.description: Always ask what picture or visual could be used to elucidate a topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals needn't be fancy, but whenever possible a relevant picture should accompany the idea. If a topic resists visualization, acknowledge that, but make an effort to find helpful imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pointless animations
rubrics_metrics.description: Every movement on screen should be deliberate with an identifiable purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure visuals and movement communicate the same point as the narration so they reinforce each other rather than competing. Avoid animating text/equations just for motion's sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content reuse: permitted short-clip use criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: You may use still images or clips from 3b1b videos only if you follow all listed criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed use requires: using less than 60 seconds of material; clearly adding to it in the surrounding context (not reuploading wholesale); clear on-screen attribution to 3Blue1Brown; and providing links where applicable so viewers can find the original. Other use cases (e.g., uploading full lessons elsewhere) require contacting for licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No re-uploads
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not re-upload the content on your own channel; such re-uploaded content will be taken down as a copyright violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy prevents inserted promotions/sponsors or edits that misrepresent the original intent; reach out via licensing inquiry for other arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributing subtitles: use Criblate
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtitles can be contributed via Criblate, which allows communities to review, edit, and add translations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once approved on Criblate, contributions are added as official YouTube subtitles for that language with attribution to the contributor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dubs and translations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Official dubs exist in several languages created by hired contractors; volunteers work to make videos available on platforms like Bilibili for regions without YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to contribute a dub in another language and have experience with math and narration, contact with a sample audio track. For Chinese availability, volunteer efforts help publish on Bilibili.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not expect research verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The author will not check claims of having solved famous unsolved math problems or verify novel research ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: not a research mathematician, limited time, and the need to draw boundaries. Do not send such claims expecting review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking requests guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The author generally has limited availability for talks but is open to hearing requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reaching out, provide date, location, and whether you have an estimated speaking fee in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship and partnership policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The channel does not do brand integrations or sponsorships in videos, though recruiting partnerships exist via 3b1b Talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other forms of commercial/brand collaboration, the stated default is to decline integrations in video content; contact about recruiting partnerships specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music usage/licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Most music is written by Vincent Rubinetti (with some piano pieces by the author); music is available on Bandcamp/Spotify/Apple Music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For usage and licensing questions about the music, follow the provided form/links to inquire.
